questions.prompt: What is the strongest migration stance for a production Next.js 16 upgrade?

options.label: Treat it as only a dependency bump if TypeScript compiles.
Treat it as a cache, request API, routing, proxy, and rollout risk review.
Rewrite all routes to Client Components before upgrading.

questions.explanation: Version 16 touches behavior that can affect correctness, not only syntax.

items.label: Record current versions and route behavior
Run official codemod in a branch
Audit cache configs, async request APIs, and proxy behavior

questions.prompt: Match the migration area to the review question.

pairs.match: which old route configs should become local cached scopes

questions.explanation: A migration review maps each changed framework area to concrete app behavior.

questions.prompt: Order release checks after the code compiles.

items.label: Run typecheck, lint, unit, and content checks
Run browser journeys for forms, auth, images, and cached routes
Monitor stale data, navigation, server errors, and build timings
Keep rollback and dependency pin path ready

questions.explanation: Release readiness combines automated checks with production observability and rollback discipline.
